quest.title: Memories of Gurabad
quest.description: There was a strange vibration in the ancient "training field" which, according to Liloupar, may have something to do with Gurabad's long past...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...Be careful. I feel some strange tremors from deep underground.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What did you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: It's nothing... That was just a drill.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So it was just a drill!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... What kind of drill are you talking about!?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Shh... They're here.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...Be careful. I feel some strange tremors from deep underground.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What did you feel?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: It's nothing... That was just a drill.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... So it was just a drill!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... What kind of drill are you talking about!?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Shh... They're here.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Please connect me with that chess piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C—Connect...? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Find the protrusion on its surface and insert that into the slot on my bottle. It's as simple as that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... there's a slot on your bottle? But it looks pretty smooth... There's no place to plug it in!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: It's there. You just can't see it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...Because I just made it up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Hey!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Ha... Alright, that's enough jokes for now. All you have to do, my master, is to hold me and touch the chess piece.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Liloupar, are you alright? Why are you so quiet?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... Look. She's glowing. Well, differently from normal, anyway...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The Jinni's bottle shimmers, seemingly in tune with the vibration of the chess piece.\nYou can hear the passing of time like drops of water in a prison... It seems to last a lifetime, or perhaps just for a moment.\nLiloupar doesn't say a word.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Then, out of the mist, you see a great city, big, bloated, and cold.\nThe earth opens up, swallowing everything in Gurabad...\nAnd there stands its gate, set in the mountain wall. It is loathsome, seeming almost to contain all the filth of the ancient world that somehow escaped the people's gaze...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: That's Gurabad over there. I remember it now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: My head really hurts...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, what's the matter with you guys... Can't you let Paimon know in advance next time? These surprises are bad for Paimon's heart!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! That's what you get for cheesing Paimon off!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #Heh... What a child you are. Worry not, I will give {M#him}{F#her} back, little one.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: #And when the time comes, {M#he}{F#she} shall see you compensated with all the food you may desire, and that... currency of yours. "Mura," was it?

choices.text: It's "Mora"... wait, what am I even correcting you for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that's more like it! Paimon's noted it all down! Delicious food and Mora!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Alright, playtime is over. Let us go to Gurabad, my master.

choices.text: Why do we have to go there?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Why, you ask? In truth, I know not... Perhaps the reason does not even matter, but I must make my way there. So...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: If there must be a reason, my master, it would be because I want you to witness my past and the lessons I learned.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This does sound kinda ridiculous... and Paimon really doesn't get it, but what you're saying almost sounds like a farewell. Did something happen?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah, nay. I just wish to show you some things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's that supposed to mean!? You're talking in riddles!

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: In short, please follow me. I shall lead you to Gurabad...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: There's nothing left. Nothing at all...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: All that remains are the memories of ghosts, broken dreams that can never be recovered, and the sweet aftertaste of revenge... or so I would say.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: This is a sizable request, and of that I am aware... but I wish for you to witness my past and the lessons I had to learn.

choices.text: Don't put words into my mouth...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's what you always say!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! We were just next to that chess piece. Then things went "whoosh," and now we're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How did this happen? That's really awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hehe, and would you like a repeat performance?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, show some restraint! What are you, a kid?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: That is normal. The coordinates are somewhat off. Perhaps the device is showing its age...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey... Isn't this the valley we first went to? What are you bringing us here for? Is there anything worth seeing here?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: You ask too many questions, little one.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Strange... It was supposed to be here... Ah, here it is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it... Paimon's head feels a little woozy, too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that you mention it... Paimon's head feels a little woozy, too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Behold Gurabad. Once, it was swallowed by the very earth itself — now, it lies before you.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Ah. It would seem that this place has some new tenants. Please do get rid of them, my master.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: "Shiruyeh is Khorramdin." \nThus says the man in the brass mask.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: "There will be no heirs to your name. I will do away with the many idols in your temples. I will consign you to your grave, for such does one as despicable as you deserve."\nSays the man in the brass mask.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Through the Jinni's entranced eyes, you bear witness to Gurabad as it is engulfed in darkness... \nThe city of Gurabad has long been a reservoir of water, but now its inhabitants scatter like a torrent. \nThe Jinn, devoid of intellect, pour out from cold machine husks, from the soldiers' weapons... And the scarlet wine, the juice of the pomegranate, bursts forth...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The pomegranates are crushed and cracked, and they are trampled into a mass of mud... Plump or withered, rich or humble... The scarlet fruits, with hue and cry, tell of the Khorramdin's coming — the joy of life and the joy of vengeance.\nThe juice tastes as sweet and mellow as sweet wine, and flows through the city, turning the reservoir into a vast red sea... \nThe sea first drowns the slaves, and then their masters howl as they flounder amidst the roiling waves of night.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Finally, you see the brass-masked king. He flees into the shadows — into Shirin's arms... \nHer face is old and dim, all traces of life and reason having vanished from it like dust in the night's wind.\nAnd then there is King Kisra, who turned into a dark monster... they all are your flesh and blood, yet you rejoice, and you exult in that retribution.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: O Gurabad, you are mortally stricken, your shame shown to all...\nAll who receive these tidings shall clap and shout for joy...\nFor is there anyone who has not felt your unending tyranny?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text:
You hold the magic bottle to your ear...
There is a chuckle, and you hear someone whispering in your ear in a gentle and delicate language...
She speaks of things as unknowable as a deep spring, but you comprehend it all.
And at last, the words dissipate, leaving only a cool tingling in your ear...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Through her guidance, you have become familiar with the ancient verses... \nBut she speaks no more.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the shard of light merges with Liloupar's magic bottle, you feel a little of your own power being pulled away...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: "O Gurabad, you are mortally stricken, your shame shown to all..."

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ormazd was once the lover of the one called Liloupar. It was by the Jinni's love that he rose from a lowly shepherd to become a king amongst mortals.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I once believed that he was no mere mortal companion. Foolishly, I fell for those eyes of his... But the vanity and selfishness that kings are wont to have seized him in the end.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: He turned out to be no different from those mortal rulers who live one day and die the next, wandering amidst dreams of conquest and persecution, building their palaces upon quicksand.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you brought him low...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Like I said, I punished him — handed ruin down from father to son, across three generations.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Kisra Parvezravan, Shirin, they are my blood... It was by schemes of blood, honeyed execution, and raging ambition that I punished them all.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: But that was not all... *sigh* That was not all.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Vain Parvezravan, my dear child... He wanted unlimited power, and so I gave it to him.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I designed for him machines driven by the remnants of Jinn spirits, and in a dream of pitch-black darkness, I inspired him to build a colossal machine that could swallow up and spit out a torrent of artificial objects...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: They brought him untold wealth, but they also robbed the laborers of their lives and the farmers of their property.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Thus the lords and the rich men wept, crying: "Verily this is the triumph of mortals, the end of slavery!" But only I knew. Only I understood...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: This abolition of slavery was itself the beginning of endless and cruel servitude — slave owners were freed from the obligation to raise their slaves, and the slaves were deprived even of small mercies like a full stomach...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, you're starting to lose Paimon here... What are you talking about!?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Poverty is accompanied by hatred, and hatred begets ambition... Riches lead to greed, and greed also fuels ambition.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: It was ambition that drove him to force his queen, Shirin — his elder sister by blood — to create Jinn, mindless and malformed... And her suffering pleased me... it empowered me...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: ...And I was thus able to foster their flesh and blood.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Yes, Shiruyeh, brass-masked Khorramdin. The smallfolk and the slaves saw him as an emissary of my mistress, as a savior to them in their misery.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: So he led them to embrace justice... To embrace death.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Hmm? So you're still here, little one... Why are you silent?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... it's just, Paimon doesn't understand... And what you just said sounded really terrifying.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Oh, it's alright... I was only talking about my past... and of my destiny.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Paimon... Paimon doesn't know what to say...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Thanks to your company, I was able to return to my mistress's garden...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what made you say this all of a sudden...?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Gurabad is, for me, a fated land. I must therefore return back to this city, where my destiny awaits me still.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Do you have to go back and make amends for all the wrong things you've done or something...?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Done wrong? Ha! I have done nothing wrong. But my children are still there. She and Shiruyeh... they must be rather lonely.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So what you're saying is...

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: The power of the darkness is growing stronger... only a mother's power can face it head-on.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: I thought I could use the dark abyss to punish that which I hated... But what goes around, comes around... It shall also be my destiny to enter Gurabad and face its retribution.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: My master... I am sorry that I couldn't stay by your side for long, and that I could not have more time to get familiar with you.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: But I know that fate will arrange for us to meet again. You possess an incorruptible quality. I believe... that I will have made the right choice.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Generally speaking, the master doesn't choose the Jinni. Instead, the Jinni chooses their master. Even should we part ways here, I doubt our connection will be easily severed.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: So... please accept this final gift.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Please... hold me close to your ear once more.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text:
You hold the magic bottle to your ear...
There is a chuckle, and you hear someone whispering in your ear in a gentle and delicate language...
She speaks of things as unknowable as a deep spring, but you comprehend it all.
And at last, the words dissipate, leaving only a cool tingling in your ear...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Through her guidance, you have become familiar with the ancient verses... \nBut she speaks no more.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, look! The light in the bottle has dimmed... Liloupar! Are you alright?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Liloupar? Liloupar?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: (The light of the bottle fades, then the flickering gradually returns — but she speaks no more.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that how it is... Seems like it really was goodbye... Will we ever see her again...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And uh, should we... go now?

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: Ah, yes... Khorramdin, brass-masked King Shiruyeh. "The Emissary of the Mistress"! "Savior of the Commoners and Slaves"! Haha. A gifted charlatan, that one.

response.speaker: Liloupar
response.text: And in the end, he led those who followed him to their doom... The earth swallowed them whole, and they fell into a dark chasm together with the entire city.
